items.title: Schuller Gunther — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: the interviewee narrates a historical account of Darius Milhaud's life and work without indicating any personal interaction or relationship with him.

ctx.x: We wanted to bring this to the present.

All this was coming together in some way. Anyway, the big breakthrough thing was, one of the greatest French composers of that time, Darius Milhaud, with whom Dave Brubeck studied out in California, later, he was invited to conduct the Philadelphia Orchestra by Leopold Stokowski, who was the conductor of that. So he came to America in 1922. He did his conducting there, one week in Philadelphia. But when he arrived, having heard about jazz from Ernest Ansermet, who was the guy who heard Sidney Bechet play in…

it down, what he thought he had heard, so that if you didn’t know this was all composed by him, you might think, wow, that sounds like they’re improvising. But of course the musicians, who then played that piece in Paris, were all classical studio musicians. They couldn’t improvise.
